rule: Design-layer controlled input. It assigns every governed visual contract (Master 11) a design tier and, for SIGNATURE and CORE_ANALYTICAL visuals, declares which governed rows a chart binds to and how they are drawn. It never carries a fact, number, label or sentence: values come from Master data rows, text from Master contract/evidence fields, and legend labels from the governed interface copy (UI-VIS-*). The generator resolves every binding and fails on any unresolved ID, any value that disagrees with its guard, or any visual left untiered.

tiers.SIGNATURE: Distinctive to this product, decision-useful, drawable from governed rows and safe when detached. Designed first; gets a full data contract.
tiers.CORE_ANALYTICAL: A standard chart form carrying governed values a reader needs. Gets a full data contract.
tiers.SUPPORTING: Secondary diagram or state figure; may be drawn once signature and core visuals are done. Its governed text alternative is the complete content until then.
tiers.TABLE_TEXT_FIRST: Rendered as the governed ordered text or a table. A drawn chart would add no truth or would need data the Master does not hold; the promotion condition is stated.
tiers.RETIRE_FROM_DESIGN: Not drawn. The Evidence Record and its text stay; Design does not build a chart for it.

grammar.rule: Colour is never the only carrier. Every state below is carried by at least two of: mark shape or fill, line style, a direct text label from the governed UI-VIS copy, and position. States never fade with age (age is not invalidity) and never use red/amber/green.

evidence_states.mark: bracket or difference annotation, never a bar of its own
evidence_states.label: value and the word 'calculated'
period printed on the mark; no fading

evidence_states.mark: outlined mark inside a labelled programme frame
evidence_states.label: programme universe printed

evidence_states.mark: empty cell with the word, never a zero-height bar or blank
evidence_states.label: always printed

structure_markers.draw: line stops; labelled gap on the time axis; the two documents are named on either side
line stops; labelled vertical rule; no connecting segment
both values at the same position on the time axis, keyed by publication, never as consecutive points
gap in the line with a labelled empty slot; never interpolated, never zero
neutral note mark (†) on every affected period, with both figures in the note; applied to every flagged row, not only the largest
outlined marker at the target date; never a progress bar unless the comparator's compatibility is governed as direct
filled marker; when no result is governed, an UNKNOWN cell
values in separate panels or axes with the label between them
label on the value axis title, always visible
no value mark and no number: the slot keeps its position and carries the governed label in place of the value; never a zero, an empty bar, an estimate or a faded mark

chain.rule: Rule-to-outcome chains run top to bottom in both languages. A step is EVIDENCED only when a governed row supports it; otherwise it is OPEN. OPEN is not failure and carries no colour of warning. Activity counts (transactions, values) evidence OPERATION, not USE: use needs a person- or firm-level measure.

display_labels.rule: Every category, series, lane, unit, event and state value that a SIGNATURE or CORE_ANALYTICAL chart prints is mapped here to governed interface copy (04 UI-VIS-CAT-*, UI-VIS-UNIT-*). The generator adds <field>_label {en, ar, ui_id} to the value or record and stops if a printed value has no label. Temporal values (years, ISO months and dates) are formatted by locale and are not labelled; fields listed as encoding_only select a mark or a chain step and are never printed. A spec may also derive a second label from a field (derived_labels, e.g. the 'is not' line of a payment object) and name governed in-frame sentences (frame_labels); both are resolved from 04 in both languages.

global_rules.detached_frame: Inside the image frame of every SIGNATURE and CORE_ANALYTICAL chart: the governed title; period and universe (from the Evidence Record when one exists); the credit line (UI-VIS-SOURCE + governed publisher); the governed prohibited inference (UI-VIS-DOES-NOT-ESTABLISH); any break, missing or disagreement marker present in the data; the canonical link (UI-VIS-FULL-RECORD). A crop that removes any of these is not a supported export.
global_rules.rtl: Numeric time axes run left to right in both languages (bilingual crops circulate side by side; a mirrored rising line reads as a fall). Text, legends, captions, panel order and categorical bar labels follow the reading direction. Chains and ladders run top to bottom. Digits are Western; IDs, currency codes, signed percentages and index-base or equation expressions (such as 2021 = 100) are isolated as left-to-right runs. Horizontal numeric value axes run left to right in both languages. No arrow glyph between numbers in Arabic text.
global_rules.mobile: At 320 and 390 CSS px (the tested narrow widths) every chart has a defined small-screen form (stated per contract). Matrices become one card per row; multi-panel figures stack; no horizontal scrolling of the plot area.
global_rules.text_alternative: Every chart ships with its analytical text alternative (the governed accessible summary plus the prohibited inference) and a table or ordered-text fallback with caption, scoped headers, unit, universe and period. The alternative must stay true if the chart fails to load.
global_rules.no_decoration: No decorative SVG, illustration, icon field or gradient carries or implies data. The static baseline draws no charts.
global_rules.axes: Bar and dot value axes start at zero. A line chart may use a non-zero value axis only with the axis origin labelled. Never draw two value axes on one plot. Never encode a value as area, bubble or icon size.

visuals.rationale: Stops the likeliest false headline in the product (a same-year restatement read as a collapse). Panel 1 draws two governed values at the same reference year, keyed by publication; panel 2 compares the CBY AR2025 path and the IMF staff-report path, each indexed to its own 2021 value, as separate lanes.

contract.form: Panel 1: two markers at reference year 2024, keyed by publication vintage (SAME_YEAR_REVISION). Panel 2: the CBY AR2025 vintage and the IMF 2025 Article IV staff report, each indexed to its own 2021 value (2021 = 100), drawn as two side-by-side small panels with their own indexed axes, one per source; the paths are never drawn on one axis, merged, joined or shown as one harmonised series. The in-frame note states that their near-identity is not independent confirmation.

panels.closed_in: Pre-Tranche-C P5.3: CBY AR2025 2021-2023 values governed in 23_REMITTANCES (primary read of SRC-CBY-AR2025-BOP).

contract.ordering: Panel 1: publication order (AR2024 value, then AR2025 restatement). Panel 2: chronological, 2021 to 2024, one lane per source.
contract.transformation: Panel 1: none; values as published (USD million), no percentage change between the two markers. Panel 2: each series is divided by its own 2021 value and multiplied by 100 (derived, DERIVED state); the indexed axis compares paths, not levels, and raw levels are shown only in the fallback table beside their own source. The growth-gap guard checks the governed claim CLM-037.
contract.breaks: Panel 1: SAME_YEAR_REVISION marker between the two values; no connecting line. Panel 2: NOT_COMPARABLE on the levels of the two lanes; no line joins one lane to the other, and neither lane is joined to the AR2024 vintage.
contract.annotation: UI-VIS-SAME-YEAR-REVISION on the panel-1 pair; UI-VIS-NOT-COMPARABLE and the unit label UI-VIS-UNIT-INDEX-2021 on panel 2; the governed prohibited inference in frame.
contract.mobile: Panel 1: two stacked labelled dots with the vintage label beside each value. Panel 2 below it: the two small panels stacked, each with its own indexed axis and source label.
contract.rtl: Vintage and lane labels mirror; numeric time and value axes stay left to right.
contract.fallback: Panel 1: two-row table (publication, reference year, value in USD million, source). Panel 2: table of year, CBY AR2025 value and index, IMF value and index, each column group with its own source.

derived.guard_of: CLM-037: maximum annual-growth difference 2022-2024 of about 0.0032 percentage points

visuals.rationale: The product's rule-to-result argument as a drawable state chain: evidence reaches rules, implementation and recorded activity; access, use, quality and outcome stay open. Vertical and mobile-native.

contract.form: Chain, top to bottom, for the payment-architecture reform as a whole; each step EVIDENCED or OPEN (grammar chain). Events are placed by chain step, not by rail: the governed event rows carry no rail field.

step_mapping.UI-VIS-CHAIN-RULE: NETWORK_RULE and PAYMENTS_ARCHITECTURE_DECISION events, and the funded project steps PROJECT_START, PAYMENT_RAIL_COMPONENT and ACCESS_USAGE_COMPONENT (a project component is a programme, not implementation)
step_mapping.UI-VIS-CHAIN-IMPLEMENTATION: NETWORK_INTEGRATION, UNIFIED_NETWORK_COMPANY and YPCC events, and the POS terminal stock (OBS-00080)
step_mapping.UI-VIS-CHAIN-OPERATION: POS transactions (OBS-00081) and NETWORK_ACTIVITY_SIGNAL; activity counts evidence operation, not use
step_mapping.UI-VIS-CHAIN-ACCESS: OPEN (the FMIIP access-point baseline is a project metric, not access by people)

contract.ordering: Steps in chain order; events within a step by date.
contract.transformation: Only the listed event IDs are drawn (the same-date, same-source duplicates REF-PAY-010 and REF-PAY-007 were merged into REF-PAY-006 and REF-PAY-013 in the Master, transaction R85-B).
contract.missing: OPEN steps are drawn as open with UI-VIS-CHAIN-OPEN; never as failure, never as a percentage.
contract.annotation: Each EVIDENCED step shows its dated event(s); the POS values print their governed object label (POS terminals, POS transactions) and unit for the latest month.
contract.mobile: Native vertical list; one card per step.
contract.rtl: Top to bottom in both languages; no horizontal arrows.
contract.fallback: Ordered list of steps with state, dated events and links.

visuals.rationale: Whose list, on what date, and what it proves, for each provider class, with no score. Distinctive, and it answers the regulator's and journalist's first question about providers.

contract.form: Matrix: one row per provider class; columns = authority source, dated named universe or count, status events, negative authority, operation evidence. Cells hold words and dates, never filled dots.
contract.ordering: Rows: banks, exchange and remittance actors, wallets and e-money, microfinance (non-bank), payment-system operators (UNKNOWN). Columns in the order above.
contract.transformation: Counts only as governed; the 429 roster total is not shown as a number of providers. Wallet counts appear as 'counts differ by source and date' with the dated values listed, never one number.
contract.missing: A dimension with no governed row is UNKNOWN (UI-VIS-STATE-UNKNOWN), e.g. negative authority for classes other than wallets ('none held', not 'none exist'); operation evidence for every class.
contract.annotation: UI-VIS-ISSUER-SCOPE in frame for the rows whose authority is Central Bank of Yemen — Aden (authority field of the status and negative-authority rows); the microfinance row's source is the Yemen Microfinance Network's membership pages.
contract.known_gap: The contract text names payment-system operators; no PUC row exists for them. The row is drawn as UNKNOWN with the institution events of 31 (REF-PAY-011..013) listed as context, not as a named universe.
contract.mobile: One card per provider class with the five dimensions as a definition list.
contract.rtl: Column order mirrors with the reading direction; dates and IDs isolated left to right.
contract.fallback: Table with caption, one row per class, scoped headers.

visuals.rationale: The latest representative people-side measure and its four same-wave gaps. Standard bars; the value is in the discipline of the frame (wave, fieldwork, coverage exclusion).

contract.form: Horizontal bars of levels; bracket annotations for the four same-wave gaps (women/men; poorest 40%/richest 60%; primary education or less/secondary education or more; ages 15–24/ages 25 and over).
contract.ordering: Total first, then women and men, then poorest 40% and richest 60%, then primary education or less and secondary education or more, then ages 15–24 and ages 25 and over.
contract.transformation: Gaps are differences of governed values in percentage points, printed as brackets, never as bars. Each gap compares two groups of the same dimension in the same wave; groups of different dimensions are never compared.
contract.missing: No intervals are drawn (none governed). The age bars use their own population bases (ages 15–24; ages 25 and over), shown in the unit label.
contract.breaks: None. No other wave is joined to this one.
contract.annotation: Fieldwork dates and the approximately 23% population coverage exclusion in frame. The governed sampling note (frame_labels) is printed in frame.
contract.mobile: Bars stack full width; brackets become text lines under each pair.
contract.rtl: Bars grow from the reading start; group labels mirror; values stay Western digits.

visuals.rationale: The IMF series with its three evidence states and the document break, so forecast revisions are not read as economic change.

contract.form: Line with reported history (solid, filled marks), estimate (hollow mark) and projections (dashed, hollow marks); BREAK_VINTAGE between 2024 and 2025.
contract.missing: The earlier staff-report forecast vintage is not held; only the supplement's estimate and projections are drawn.
contract.breaks: BREAK_VINTAGE where source_id changes (staff report to supplement); the line is not joined.
contract.annotation: Scope in frame: IMF analytical scope for areas under the internationally recognized government (Evidence Record universe).
contract.mobile: Full-width line; state labels placed directly on the three segments.
contract.rtl: Time axis left to right; labels mirror.
contract.fallback: Table: year, value, state, source document.

visuals.rationale: Monthly administrative counts with every source-internal disagreement marked the same way. Drawn as panel 1 of the POS small multiple.

contract.form: Line of monthly counts; panel 1 of a three-panel small multiple with VIS-POS-TRANSACTIONS and VIS-POS-VALUE (separate value axes, never one axis).
contract.missing: Any expected month without a row is MISSING.
contract.annotation: DISAGREEMENT note mark on every flagged month; note text from the passport critical limit (EP-CBY-POS-MONTHLY).
contract.mobile: Panels stack vertically; each keeps its own axis and title.
contract.rtl: Time axis left to right; titles mirror.

visuals.rationale: Panel 2 of the POS small multiple. The path is not steady (July 2025 high), which endpoint framing hid.

contract.form: Line of monthly transaction counts; panel 2 of the POS small multiple.
contract.transformation: None; raw monthly totals. Transactions per terminal is not drawn (not a governed object).
contract.missing: Any expected month without a row is MISSING.
contract.annotation: DISAGREEMENT note mark on every flagged month; the monthly high is labelled directly.

visuals.rationale: Panel 3 of the POS small multiple: nominal value with the missing month kept missing.

contract.form: Line of nominal monthly value; panel 3 of the POS small multiple; NOMINAL on the axis title.
contract.transformation: None; nominal YER million. No price or exchange-rate adjustment and no exchange-rate annotation (it would invite a causal reading).
contract.missing: September 2025 is MISSING: gap in the line, labelled.
contract.annotation: UI-VIS-NOMINAL on the axis; MISSING label on September 2025.
contract.fallback: Table: month, value (YER million) or 'no verified value'.

visuals.rationale: Keeps cards, accounts, subscribers, terminals and transactions as different objects before any comparison. Card-first; no totals.

contract.form: One card per measurement object, each with its 'is not' line; no totals row, no population denominator.

series.withhold_when_caveat_matches: require methodology note before public use

contract.ordering: Series order: cards, ATMs, e-wallets, e-wallet subscribers, POS terminals, POS transactions, accounts.
contract.transformation: None. No card is summed with another or divided by population.
contract.missing: Values whose governed caveat requires a methodology note before public use are withheld (UI-VIS-WITHHELD): the object card shows what it counts, not the number.
contract.breaks: Flagged objects carry NOT_COMPARABLE and the card note UI-VIS-NOTE-NOT-COMPARABLE-2024Q3: no comparison with the 2024 Q3 bulletin is drawn. Cards have no line, so no line-break marker is printed.
contract.annotation: Each card prints its governed object label (x_label) and its governed 'is not' line (is_not_label). The caveat field is an internal comparability note and is not printed; the frame prints the governed marker labels instead.
contract.fallback: Table: object, value or withheld state, what it is not.

visuals.rationale: Quoted costs by corridor and send amount: a small, decision-useful comparison with the scale effect visible.

contract.form: Dot plot: two corridors × two send amounts; the amount is an explicit axis, never pooled.
contract.missing: Provider and quote counts are not held; not drawn.
contract.annotation: Quarter and the governed note UI-VIS-RPW-AVERAGE-NOTE (frame_labels) in frame.
contract.rtl: Value axis left to right; labels mirror.

visuals.rationale: The 31 firms with a line of credit out of 328 (FFO-2022-004) and the 18 valid loan-source responses (FFO-2022-LS-01..04) are rendered as a table (stage, count, base). Two stages drawn in sequence would read as a funnel, which requires the 18 responses to come from the 31 firms; the Master does not establish that.
visuals.promotion_requires: The Master states whether the 18 loan-source responses are a subset of the 31 firms with a line of credit.

visuals.rationale: Places access to finance among the constraints firms named, without a rank or a national claim.

contract.form: Horizontal bars sorted by share, no rank numbers; multi-response note in frame.
contract.ordering: By share, descending, without rank numbers.
contract.transformation: None. The eight items named in the governed contract are drawn; the other eight governed items (FFO-2022-CH-09..16) appear in the table fallback.
contract.missing: The base for this question is not held; stated in frame.
contract.annotation: Firms could name more than one challenge (shares add to more than 100%); seven-governorate survey; not a national ranking.

visuals.rationale: Borrowers, savers and nominal portfolio at three dated anchors (21_MFI_DATA spine rows SRC-SFD-Q4-2015-001, SRC-SFD-Q4-2020-001, SRC-SANAA-MFB-2024) are not comparable enough to draw: saver definitions differ, the rial valuation of the portfolio figures is not recorded, and the 2023 anchor is a secondary sector figure whose provider set is not verified (UI-VIS-NOTE-MFI-2023-SECONDARY). Rendered as a table: date, borrowers, savers, portfolio (YER million) and the evidence state of each value. RV-CWR-006 uses the same table.
visuals.promotion_requires: A governed saver-definition crosswalk and a governed rial-valuation field on each portfolio anchor (Master-first).

visuals.rationale: The FMIIP access-point baseline and target (FMIIP-RF-004) and the result, which is not held, are rendered as a three-row table (state, date, value). Two markers on a dated axis would invite a trajectory that no observation supports.
visuals.promotion_requires: An observed result for the same indicator under the project's own definition (FMIIP-RF-004), Master-first.

visuals.rationale: Parallel dated lanes show that people-side evidence (2022–23 fieldwork) and system evidence (2025–26) are asynchronous, ending in an open population-outcome node. The drawable instance of the evidence-clock idea.

contract.form: Three dated lanes on one time axis (people, infrastructure, institutions/reform) ending in an OPEN outcome node.
contract.ordering: Chronological on a shared axis; the people lane shows the fieldwork span (7 Nov 2022 – 9 Jan 2023, from CLM-001), not a single year.
contract.transformation: Lanes never share a value axis. Every lane, including infrastructure, is plotted as dated presence (monthly ticks for the infrastructure lane), not magnitude; only the first and the latest infrastructure values are labelled, with their governed object label. No lane has a value axis.
contract.missing: No people-side observation after the fieldwork span: the lane ends and the outcome node is OPEN.
contract.annotation: UI-VIS-CHAIN-OPEN on the final node. The people lane is drawn as the fieldwork span stated in the governed period of evidence record CLM-001, not as a point at the data year of the Findex row; the span ends the lane. Lane titles are the three governed frame labels, in lane order (people, infrastructure, institutions and reforms).
contract.mobile: Lanes become a dated vertical list.
contract.rtl: Time axis left to right; lane labels mirror.
contract.fallback: Table: lane, date, what is recorded.

visuals.rationale: Regulatory stack as cards; state-only and drawable from 31 e-money rows, but the text already carries it and ceilings pack several values per cell (EMR-007..009).
An ordered path of rule-stated time limits with an open performance node; clear as a short ordered list, and a drawn path adds little.
Four-rung ladder whose population-capability rung has no Yemen value; a state ladder, secondary to the people-side core visual.
Method explainer on /evidence/; categorical and state-only. Drawn, if at all, as unordered category cards: the classes are not a ranking.

State timeline of payment reforms; overlaps the RV-CWR-009 signature chain, whose deduplicated event set it should reuse. Its lineage is BOUND_EXACT: REF-PAY-001 was closed to SRC-CBY-DEC-23-2024-001 in P5.
Same-period banking positions across a method break: the values are not held as rows (PARTIAL), so the Reading's text carries it until they are promoted Master-first.
Measurement lanes for people, accounts, activity and infrastructure; VIS-PAYMENT-ANATOMY carries the core of it.
Historical five-provider e-money figures; PARTIAL (transaction-value mix held only as text).
Uses the VIS-MFI-DIVERGENCE table of dated anchors (TABLE_TEXT_FIRST); draws no separate chart.
Levels are those of VIS-FINDEX-GAPS; the hypotheses layer is a text list, not arrows.
Three bases in three panels; reuses the firm core visuals plus the SMEPS KPI (CLM-060). PARTIAL until the SMEPS values are rows.
Transfer-to-persistence ladder; state-only, the persistence link is open.

13_SYSTEM_RELATIONSHIPS holds relationship statements, not evidenced links: 21 of 26 carry no reference and none carries an evidence strength. Design renders it as the ordered list of documented relationships (SL-001..010, SL-022..026) with what each does not establish; SL-011..021 are measurement, placement and navigation links, not system relationships. The current static baseline shows the governed text alternative only.
visuals.promotion_requires: An evidence reference and a governed evidence state on each system relationship (13), Master-first.

visuals.rationale: The right idea, not drawable: periods exist only as free text (97 distinct strings), with no separate observation, fieldwork, publication or retrieval dates, and retrieval dates are held for 1 of 159 sources. RV-CWR-004 is the drawable instance meanwhile.
visuals.promotion_requires: Structured observation_start, observation_end, fieldwork_start/end, publication_date and evidence_class on each public Evidence Record (06), Master-first; then SIGNATURE.

visuals.rationale: Gap types are not a governed field; the Measurement Agenda already renders each blocked evidence item as text.
visuals.promotion_requires: A typed gap field on 10_MEASUREMENT_AGENDA rows.

visuals.rationale: Implemented as the Compare tool (governed comparison fields, text-labelled states); a table by nature.
Two percentages inside a filtered base; a sentence carries them better than a stacked bar, which invites a prevalence reading.
State list of consumer-protection steps; overlaps VIS-FCP-REDRESS-PATH on the same page.
The Master uses 16 relationship types where the contract names 4; rendered as a per-record list of documented links until the taxonomy is reconciled.
visuals.promotion_requires: Contract edge types reconciled with the governed relationship taxonomy (Master).

visuals.rationale: Method contract: no operating-provider map may be drawn from lists until the access-point register (MA-005) exists.

Its data (35 OCHA FTS flows) are governed HUMANITARIAN_CONTEXT_ONLY and 'backend/context only'; a public relationship graph would present context-only data as a public analytical object. The Evidence Record text stays.
